newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ATLANTA'S YOUNG TELLS CAPE OLYMPICS BOOST BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: ATLANTA'S YOUNG TELLS CAPE OLYMPICS BOOST BUSINESS.

text.p: Atlanta Mayor Andrew Young told South African business leaders on Tuesday the Olympic Games were the best thing that had happened to his city and said Cape Town could expect a major economic boost if it hosted them in 2004.
"The city of Atlanta is virtually unanimous that the best thing that has ever happened in the life of the city is the Centennial Olympic Games," Young told a lunch meeting in Cape Town.
Young, who as U.S. ambassador to the United Nations played a key role in the diplomatic fight against apartheid, is heading a delegation of Atlanta business leaders on a visit to South Africa.
"The debate is not whether or not the Games were a success financially ... We know we brought $1.8 billion of new money into our community.
"We know that generated a tremendous amount of private investment and spin-off opportunity... The debate is whether that sum is $4.0 billion of new money or $5.0 billion," Young said.
"You multiply that into rand and you realise what is possible."
Young said the economic boost provided by hosting the Games in Cape Town would benefit all southern Africa.
"I see the Olympics in 2004 as the beginning of the discovery of the southern African marketplace...

"Given access to technology, given the infusion of new capital, given the implementation of democracy and empowerment in the midst of the economic growth that is potential around the Olympics, I think we will see this region as the opportunity and growth region for the global economy in the 21st Century," Young said.
